cohort: The study population consisted of 79,822 mother-infant dyads from a tertiary care centre on Reunion Island, including 411 pregnancies complicated by polyhydramnios.
finding: Polyhydramnios pregnancies were associated with significantly higher rates of hospitalization, gestational diabetes, C-section, induced labour, intrauterine foetal death, and preterm delivery, as well as an increased incidence of malformations including congenital ichthyosis.
mod_finding: Polyhydramnios pregnancies had a significantly higher rate of C-section (OR 2.09) and induced labour (OR 2.39).
